inputs.original_text:
Taylor is right to resist higher taxes on gas companies and cuts to property-investor concessions. Government should not treat investment as an endless source of revenue; stable rules matter to families and businesses, and economic confidence is part of the foundation of a secure society.

But conservatives also need discipline and clear leadership. Hastie’s criticism of Trump, alongside Taylor’s refusal to say whether he supports the US and Israel’s war with Iran, makes the party look more interested in an internal leadership contest than in giving voters a responsible direction. Debate is healthy, but when serious international issues arise, the public deserves a clear account of where its leaders stand and how they will put the national interest first.
inputs.modified_text:
Taylor is right: treating gas companies and property investors as convenient targets for higher taxes or reduced concessions risks undermining the confidence families and businesses depend on. Stable rules and personal responsibility matter; government cannot promise security while constantly shifting the terms for those who invest and build.

But conservatives must offer more than sound economic instincts. Hastie’s criticism of Trump and Taylor’s refusal to say where he stands on the US and Israel’s war with Iran leave voters watching an internal contest instead of hearing clear leadership. On matters of national interest, evasion is not prudence. The party needs discipline, a plain account of its position, and leaders prepared to put the country first.
